outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
outline.description: Establishes the motivation for controlling powerful text-to-image diffusion models and introduces the two downstream tasks targeted by the paper. Summarizes the shortcomings of text-only guidance and defines the desiderata for effective finetuning.
subtopics: Why text guidance is insufficient for fine-grained control
Two target tasks: subject-driven generation and controllable generation
Desiderata for finetuning: training efficiency and generalizability preservation
Pitfalls of naive finetuning: model collapse, overfitting, loss of diversity
High-level overview of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) and its constrained variant (COFT)

outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Diffusion Models and Latent Text-to-Image Systems
outline.description: Provides the necessary background on diffusion models and the architectures commonly used in text-to-image systems, with emphasis on Stable Diffusion as the experimental backbone.
subtopics: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models: forward and reverse processes
Latent vs pixel-space diffusion (e.g., Stable Diffusion, Imagen, GLIDE)
Text conditioning: CLIP and frozen text encoders in T2I systems
U-Net backbones, attention layers, and conditioning mechanisms
Where control enters the pipeline: additional conditions and adapters

outline.chapter_title: Finetuning Strategies for Large Generative Models
outline.description: Surveys mainstream finetuning techniques and their limitations when applied to text-to-image diffusion models, setting the stage for OFT.
subtopics: Standard finetuning with small learning rates: implicit Euclidean proximity
Adapter-based methods and parameter-efficient finetuning
LoRA: low-rank additive updates and their assumptions
DreamBooth for subject-driven generation
ControlNet and T2I-Adapter for controllable generation
Limitations: lack of structural guarantees and stability issues

outline.chapter_title: Geometry of Neural Representations: Angles, Hyperspheres, and Energy
outline.description: Develops the geometric perspective underpinning OFT, explaining why angular information captures semantics and how hyperspherical energy measures pairwise neuron relationships.
subtopics: Angular features and cosine similarity as semantic carriers
Hyperspherical representations: normalizing neurons to the unit sphere
Hyperspherical energy: definition, intuition, and uniformity
Invariance of pairwise angles under orthogonal transforms
Toy evidence: magnitude vs angle in autoencoders
Fourier-phase analogy: phase preserves semantics more than magnitude

outline.chapter_title: Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): Theory and Core Mechanism
outline.description: Formalizes OFT and shows how it provably preserves hyperspherical energy by applying layer-shared orthogonal transforms to neurons, maintaining semantic structure while allowing controlled adaptation.
subtopics: OFT as learning a layer-shared orthogonal matrix acting on pretrained weights
Preserving pairwise angles and hyperspherical energy exactly
Interpretation as changing the coordinate system of neurons
Comparison to minimizing Euclidean deviation alone
Connections and contrasts to orthogonal over-parameterized training (classification vs finetuning)
Why OFT balances flexibility and regularity for stable adaptation

outline.description: Details practical parameterizations of orthogonal matrices that make OFT efficient and scalable, and analyzes parameter counts relative to LoRA.
subtopics: Cayley transform for differentiable orthogonal matrices
Special orthogonal group and determinant considerations
Block-diagonal orthogonal matrices for parameter efficiency
Optional block sharing across channels or heads
Complexity analysis: O(d^2), O(d^2/r), and shared-block variants
Parameter-efficiency comparison with LoRA via concrete examples

outline.chapter_title: Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT): Stability via Radius Control
outline.description: Introduces COFT, which further constrains OFT updates to remain within a radius from identity, improving stability and reducing sensitivity to learning dynamics.
subtopics: Motivation: explicit deviation constraint in addition to orthogonality
COFT forward pass and identity initialization
Neumann series approximation to constrain Cayley parameters
Projected gradient descent on skew-symmetric parameters
Effect of epsilon: flexibility-stability trade-off and behavior limits
Empirical stability benefits and convergence smoothing

outline.chapter_title: Extensions and Applicability: Re-scaled OFT and Layer Choices
outline.description: Presents practical extensions to OFT for increased flexibility and discusses where to apply OFT within diffusion architectures.
subtopics: Re-scaled OFT: learning a per-neuron positive scaling without affecting energy
Applying OFT to attention weights (fair comparison to LoRA)
Applying OFT to convolutional layers: depth-wise and shared-block views
Architectural agnosticism: transformers, CNNs, and hybrids
Compositionality potential: chaining orthogonal transforms across tasks

outline.description: Provides a step-by-step guide to implementing OFT and COFT in practice, including initialization, hyperparameter choices, and inference deployment.
subtopics: Integrating OFT into Stable Diffusion v1.5
Initialization of orthogonal and scaling parameters
Choosing block count, block sharing, and learning rates
Selecting epsilon in COFT; sensitivity and heuristics
Data efficiency: few images for subject-driven and partial datasets for control
Baking in R at inference for zero overhead

outline.chapter_title: Subject-Driven Generation: Methods, Metrics, and Results
outline.description: Examines OFT and COFT for subject-driven generation, comparing against DreamBooth and LoRA in terms of identity preservation, prompt fidelity, diversity, convergence, and stability.
subtopics: Training setup following DreamBooth, identical losses and layers
Metrics: DINO and CLIP-I for subject fidelity, CLIP-T for prompt fidelity, LPIPS for diversity
Convergence behavior and insensitivity to iteration count
Qualitative examples: identity preservation and prompt adherence
Failure modes and how COFT mitigates collapse
Human evaluation insights (where applicable)

outline.chapter_title: Controllable Generation: Tasks, Consistency Metrics, and Comparisons
outline.description: Evaluates OFT and COFT on controllable generation tasks and introduces control consistency metrics. Compares against ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, and LoRA in convergence and final quality.
subtopics: Control tasks: edges to image (COCO), segmentation to image (ADE20K), landmarks to face (CelebA-HQ)
Control consistency metrics: IoU and F1 for edges, mean IoU and accuracies for segmentation, landmark L2 errors for faces
Convergence curves: faster and smoother behavior than baselines
Qualitative comparisons: fidelity, geometry, and adherence to control signals
Data and parameter efficiency relative to adapter-style methods
No added inference cost vs adapter-based approaches

outline.description: Reflects on why OFT works, its broader implications, and open research problems highlighted by the paper.
subtopics: Why OFT converges faster: angular updates and smooth manifold optimization
Flexibility vs regularity: role of orthogonality and block structure
Limitations: Cayley inverse cost, block-diagonal bias
Scalability and alternative orthogonal parameterizations
Compositional finetuning: multiplying orthogonal transforms across tasks
Safety and responsible use: controllability, bias, and misuse considerations
